regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Capecitabine is chemotherapy taken as tablets. NCCP 00216 covers several colorectal and breast cancer settings, including treatment after surgery and treatment of advanced disease. Ask which aim and duration apply to you.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: After you swallow capecitabine, your body changes it into fluorouracil. This interferes with the DNA and RNA processes cells use to grow. Normal cells can also be affected, which helps explain mouth soreness, bowel symptoms and changes in blood counts.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14, then no capecitabine on Days 15–21. Follow your individual prescription.
key_points: Current toxicity and recurrence guide different decisions

evidence_audit.coverage_summary: X-ACT randomised 1,987 patients after surgery for stage III colon cancer. It compared 24 weeks of capecitabine with bolus fluorouracil/folinic acid.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: This batch adds a structured foundational trial; it is not a complete contemporary sequencing guideline.
remaining_uncertainties: With median follow-up of 6.9 years, capecitabine met the trial’s non-inferiority criteria. Breast, stage II colon and resected-metastatic indications need their own evidence discussion; X-ACT is stage III colon evidence only.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Capecitabine tablets are given with pelvic radiotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer. The tablets help the radiation treatment work; your team confirms how this fits with surgery and other treatment.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: After you swallow capecitabine, your body changes it into fluorouracil. This interferes with the DNA and RNA processes cells use to grow. Normal cells can also be affected, which helps explain mouth soreness, bowel symptoms and changes in blood counts. Radiation is directed at the planned area. Capecitabine helps sensitise cancer cells to it. Nearby bowel, bladder and skin may also become irritated. Effects can build over the weeks and may continue after the final session.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–5 of each 7-day cycle, alongside radiotherapy, for up to 5–6 cycles. Follow the written plan for treatment days and interruptions.
key_points: Current toxicity and recurrence guide different decisions
Radiotherapy schedule and medical oncology decisions require coordination

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This combination treats metastatic or unresectable colorectal cancer when an irinotecan- or oxaliplatin-based combination is unsuitable. Its aims may include cancer control, symptom relief and longer survival.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic or unresectable colorectal cancer when irinotecan- or oxaliplatin-combination chemotherapy is unsuitable.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: After you swallow capecitabine, your body changes it into fluorouracil. This interferes with the DNA and RNA processes cells use to grow. Normal cells can also be affected, which helps explain mouth soreness, bowel symptoms and changes in blood counts. Bevacizumab binds VEGF, a signal that helps blood vessels grow. Blocking it can restrict the blood supply supporting a tumour. It also affects normal blood vessels and healing, which is why blood pressure, urine and planned procedures matter.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Bevacizumab infusion on Day 1; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14, then no capecitabine on Days 15–21. Follow your individual prescription.
key_points: Current toxicity and recurrence guide different decisions
NCCP 00623 renal source discrepancy requires pharmacy/consultant resolution

indications_reviewed: Metastatic or unresectable colorectal cancer when irinotecan- or oxaliplatin-combination chemotherapy is unsuitable.
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: AVEX randomised 280 people aged 70 or older with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer who were unsuitable for oxaliplatin- or irinotecan-based combinations.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: This batch adds a structured foundational trial; it is not a complete contemporary sequencing guideline.
remaining_uncertainties: Progression-free survival HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.41–0.69); the median difference was four months, with more severe treatment-related toxicity. This is not a guaranteed individual gain in survival. AVEX used capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily; NCCP 00623 lists 1250 mg/m² with a lower-start option.
